mainTopic: A חרש divorcing with a גט and the חכמים' dispute with רבן שמעון בן גמליאל; then a new משנה on whether a husband's spoken instructions for a גט can be passed through an agent (רבי מאיר vs. רבי יוסי).
overview: The עמוד opens by finishing a discussion about how a חרש יבם can divorce his יבמה. A משנה in יבמות allows deaf-mute brothers to do יבום and later divorce, with no special decree. Because of that משנה, the גמרא drops its second answer and returns to its first. רבי יוחנן then reports that the חכמים disagree with רבן שמעון בן גמליאל and do not accept a deaf-mute's written instructions. אביי tries to prove this from the word 'עולמית' (never) in a משנה. רב פפא shows that the word can be read two other ways. One reading follows רבי יצחק: a שוטה wife can be divorced by Torah law and is blocked only by the חכמים. A new משנה follows: if the husband only said 'Write' and middlemen instructed the סופר and עדים, the גט is void. The גמרא asks whether this משנה follows רבי מאיר or רבי יוסי on passing spoken instructions to an agent. It tests several readings against the משנה's wording. The עמוד ends with רב חסדא asking whose view a related משנה follows, and his answer comes on the next עמוד.

steps.title: Quoting a משנה about brothers married to sisters
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins a challenge by quoting a משנה about pairs of brothers married to pairs of sisters, where one or more of them is a חרש.
steps.simpleTranslation: But didn't we learn in a משנה: Two deaf-mute brothers married to two competent sisters, or to two deaf-mute sisters, or to two sisters where one is competent and one is deaf-mute. And likewise two deaf-mute sisters married to two competent brothers, or to two deaf-mute brothers, or to two brothers where one is competent and one is deaf-mute. All these women are exempt from חליצה and from יבום.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a challenge by quoting a משנה. The key line that creates the difficulty comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה lists every mix of deaf-mute and competent brothers and sisters. When one brother dies without children, his widow is the sister of the living brother's wife. A man may not marry his wife's sister, so she is exempt from both יבום and חליצה. This background sets up the contrast in the next line.

keyTerms.meaning: A deaf-mute, who is not considered halachically competent
A competent person who can hear and speak
The ceremony that releases a יבמה from the יבם
Levirate marriage: marrying the childless widow of one's brother

phrases.english: But didn't we learn in a mishna:
phrases.notes: This משנה is in יבמות, דף קיב:.

phrases.english: Two deaf-mute brothers
married to two competent sisters,
or to two deaf-mute sisters,

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ שְׁתֵּי אֲחָיוֹת אַחַת פִּיקַּחַת וְאַחַת חֵרֶשֶׁת;
phrases.english: or to two sisters, one competent and one deaf-mute;
and similarly, two deaf-mute sisters
married to two competent brothers,
or to two deaf-mute brothers,

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ לִשְׁנֵי אַחִין אֶחָד פִּיקֵּחַ וְאֶחָד חֵרֵשׁ –
phrases.english: or to two brothers, one competent and one deaf-mute,

phrases.aramaic: הֲרֵי אֵלּוּ פְּטוּרוֹת מִן הַחֲלִיצָה וּמִן הַיִּבּוּם.
phrases.english: these women are exempt from ḥalitza and from levirate marriage.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָתְנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a challenge against the second answer given on the previous עמוד.
steps.kashyaTarget: The alternative answer from the previous עמוד about how a deaf-mute יבם divorces his יבמה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Quoting a משנה whose general ruling, finished in the next step, does not fit that answer.

steps.title: Unrelated women may be married and later divorced
steps.stepSummary: The משנה continues: if the women were not sisters, the brothers do יבום with them and may later divorce them. This general rule is what creates the difficulty.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if the women were unrelated, the brothers marry them through יבום. And if they want to divorce them, they may divorce them.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the line of the משנה that makes the challenge. It says that when there is no sister problem, the brothers, deaf-mute ones included, do יבום and may later divorce with a גט.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה states this as a blanket rule. It covers even a deaf-mute brother whose deceased brother was also a deaf-mute, and it does not mention any special decree against divorcing in that case. That general wording does not fit the second answer from the previous עמוד, so the challenge stands.

keyTerms.meaning: Here: unrelated women, meaning not sisters to each other
They may 'enter', meaning marry them through יבום
To send them out, meaning to divorce them

steps.confusionAlert: נכריות here does NOT mean non-Jewish women. It only means the women are not related to each other, so the sister problem does not apply.

phrases.english: And if they were unrelated women, they may marry them;
and if they wanted to divorce them, they may divorce them.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִם הָיוּ נׇכְרִיּוֹת, יִכָּנְסוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the quoted משנה with the line that drives the challenge.
steps.kashyaTarget: The alternative answer from the previous עמוד
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה gives a general permission for deaf-mute brothers to divorce after יבום, with no decree mentioned, which clashes with the second answer's reasoning.

steps.title: Returning to the first answer
steps.stepSummary: Because the second answer fails, the גמרא concludes that the first answer it gave is the right one.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it is clear as we answered at first.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא drops the second answer and goes back to its original answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first answer said the case is a יבמה who was married to a competent brother and then fell to a יבם who was a deaf-mute from birth. Since the משנה from יבמות knocked out the alternative, only the first explanation is left standing.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, it is clear. This formula shows a rejected approach is being dropped.
As we answered at the beginning

steps.whatToRemember: The גמרא ends this section with its first answer: the case is a יבמה of a competent brother who fell to a יבם who was deaf-mute from birth. The second answer is rejected because of the משנה in יבמות.

phrases.english: Rather, it is clear
as we answered initially.
phrases.notes: This points back to the first answer given earlier, on the previous עמוד.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא מְחַוַּורְתָּא כִּדְשַׁנִּין מֵעִיקָּרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Accepts the challenge of steps 1-2 and goes back to the original answer.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The second answer is rejected. The first answer, a יבמה of a competent brother who fell to a יבם who was deaf-mute from birth, stands.

steps.title: The חכמים disagree with רבן שמעון בן גמליאל
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן reports that the other חכמים argue with רבן שמעון בן גמליאל on this issue.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן says: His colleagues disagree with רבן שמעון בן גמליאל.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן adds a new statement: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's view is not the only view, because his colleagues argue with him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל gave validity to a deaf-mute's written instructions. רבי יוחנן tells us his colleagues hold that a deaf-mute's writing has no halachic force. So רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's ruling is a minority position that is disputed.

keyTerms.meaning: His colleagues, the other חכמים of his generation

steps.whyThisMatters: Knowing that רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's view is disputed matters for how the גמרא will treat writing from a deaf-mute in the coming discussion.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yoḥanan says:
His colleagues disagree with him,
with Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: חֲלוּקִין עָלָיו חֲבֵירָיו עַל רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the יבום discussion to a report about a dispute over רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's view.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The colleagues of רבן שמעון בן גמליאל disagree with him and hold that written instructions from a deaf-mute have no validity.

steps.title: אביי brings support from a משנה that says 'never'
steps.stepSummary: אביי quotes a משנה: if the husband became a חרש or שוטה, he can 'never' divorce. He argues that 'never' means even if he can communicate in writing.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: We also learned this in a משנה. If the wife became a שוטה, the husband should not divorce her. If he became a חרש or a שוטה, he can never divorce her. What does 'never' mean? Doesn't it mean even though he can communicate through writing?
steps.whatsHappening: אביי is bringing a proof for רבי יוחנן's report that the חכמים disagree with רבן שמעון בן גמליאל. He shows a משנה that seems to say writing does not help a man who became a חרש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה adds the extra word 'עולמית' (never) only for the husband. אביי says this extra word must be teaching something: even a man who can write out his wishes still cannot divorce. That matches the חכמים, who argue with רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, who allows writing.

keyTerms.meaning: We also learned this in a משנה (a formula that brings support)
He became a חרש (deaf-mute) after the marriage

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי, אַף אֲנַן נָמֵי תְּנֵינָא:
phrases.english: Abaye said: We too have learned this:
If she became an imbecile, he should not divorce her.
phrases.notes: This is a משנה in יבמות 112b.

phrases.english: If he became a deaf-mute or an imbecile,
he can never divorce her.
What does 'never' mean?

phrases.aramaic: לָאו – אַף עַל גַּב דְּיָכוֹל לְדַבֵּר מִתּוֹךְ הַכְּתָב?
phrases.english: Doesn't it mean even though he can speak through writing?
phrases.notes: Literally 'speak from the writing.' He means he can make his wishes clear by writing them down.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַף אֲנַן נָמֵי תְּנֵינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a proof from a משנה for רבי יוחנן's report in step 4.
steps.raayaObject: That the חכמים disagree with רבן שמעון בן גמליאל and do not let a man who became a חרש divorce through writing.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה in יבמות: 'נתחרש הוא או נשתטה לא יוציא עולמית,' read through the extra word עולמית.

steps.title: רב פפא: without רבי יוחנן, the משנה could be read differently
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא says that without רבי יוחנן's report, he would have said רבן שמעון בן גמליאל only explains the תנא קמא. On that reading, 'never' means even if we see he is sharp, and it says nothing about writing.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: If רבי יוחנן had not taught us this, I would have said that רבן שמעון בן גמליאל came only to explain the reason of the תנא קמא. Then what does 'never' mean? Even though we see that he is sharp.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא is pushing back on אביי's proof. He shows that the word 'never' in the משנה can be read another way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If 'never' means 'even though he seems sharp,' then the משנה only rules out judging the man by how clever he appears. It says nothing against writing. So the משנה does not prove a disagreement. We know there is a disagreement only because רבי יוחנן told us so.

keyTerms.meaning: The first, unnamed opinion in a משנה or ברייתא
To explain the reason (not to argue)

steps.confusionAlert: רב פפא is not denying that there is a disagreement. He accepts רבי יוחנן's report. He only says that אביי's משנה does not prove it.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא: אִי לָאו דְּאַשְׁמְעִינַן רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן,
phrases.english: Rav Pappa said: If Rabbi Yochanan had not taught us,
phrases.notes: He means רבי יוחנן's report in step 4 that the חכמים argue.

phrases.aramaic: הֲוָה אָמֵינָא רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל
phrases.english: I would have said that Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel

phrases.aramaic: לְפָרוֹשֵׁי טַעְמָא דְּתַנָּא קַמָּא הוּא דַּאֲתָא;
phrases.english: came to explain the reason of the first tanna;
and what does 'never' mean?

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל גַּב דַּחֲזֵינָא לֵיהּ דְּחָרִיף.
phrases.english: Even though we see that he is sharp.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי לָאו דְּאַשְׁמְעִינַן רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן הֲוָה אָמֵינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects אביי's proof by reading עולמית differently.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the proof from the משנה. It does not reject רבי יוחנן's report of a disagreement.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The word עולמית can mean 'even if he seems sharp,' so it need not refer to writing.

steps.title: Another reading: 'never' contrasts the husband with the wife, following רבי יצחק
steps.stepSummary: Another reading: the משנה says 'never' only for the husband to set him apart from the wife. By Torah law a שוטה wife can be divorced, as רבי יצחק teaches.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or else, 'never' comes to teach like רבי יצחק. רבי יצחק said: By Torah law, a שוטה can be divorced, just like a mentally competent woman, who can be divorced against her will.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא gives a second way to explain the word 'never' without bringing in writing. It is there to contrast the husband's case with the wife's case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When the wife becomes a שוטה, the ban on divorce is only from the חכמים, because by Torah law a woman can be divorced without her consent. When the husband becomes a חרש or שוטה, he truly cannot divorce, even by Torah law. The word 'never' marks this difference. So it does not prove anything about writing.

phrases.english: Alternatively, it is for the teaching of Rabbi Yitzchak,
as Rabbi Yitzchak said:
By Torah law, an imbecile woman can be divorced,
just like a competent woman, who can be divorced against her will.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי נָמֵי, לְכִדְרַבִּי יִצְחָק
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second reading of עולמית that also weakens אביי's proof.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the proof from עולמית.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: עולמית is needed to contrast the husband's Torah-level inability with the wife's rabbinic-level ban, not to rule out writing.

steps.title: Why the חכמים blocked divorcing a שוטה wife
steps.stepSummary: רבי יצחק explains why the חכמים said a שוטה wife may not be divorced: so that people will not treat her as ownerless.
steps.simpleTranslation: So why did they say she may not be divorced? So that people will not treat her as ownerless.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes רבי יצחק's teaching. It gives the reason for the rule of the חכמים that blocks divorcing a שוטה wife.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Torah allows the divorce, but the חכמים forbade it to protect her. Without a husband, and without the ability to protect herself, she could be taken advantage of. This shows that her ban is only rabbinic, unlike the husband's ban, which is from the Torah. That difference is why 'never' appears only for him.
steps.whatToRemember: אביי tried to prove from the word 'עולמית' that a man who became a חרש cannot divorce even by writing. רב פפא answered that 'עולמית' can mean either 'even if he seems sharp' or 'unlike the wife.' A שוטה wife can be divorced by Torah law, and is blocked only by the חכמים to protect her.

phrases.english: And what is the reason they said she cannot be divorced?
phrases.notes: 'They' means the חכמים, whose rule appears in the משנה: 'נשטית לא יוציא.'

phrases.english: So that people will not treat her as ownerless.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמָה טַעַם אָמְרוּ אֵינָהּ מִתְגָּרֶשֶׁת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes רבי יצחק's teaching by giving the reason for the rabbinic ban.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The ban on divorcing a שוטה wife is from the חכמים, so that she will not be treated as ownerless.

steps.title: New משנה: The Husband Only Said 'Write'
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that if the husband only told people to 'write' a גט, and they told a סופר and עדים what to do, the גט is void unless the husband himself instructs the סופר and the עדים.
steps.simpleTranslation: People asked a husband: 'Shall we write a גט for your wife?' He answered: 'Write.' They told a סופר, who wrote it, and told עדים, who signed it. Even if they wrote it, signed it, gave it to the husband, and he gave it to his wife, the גט is void. It only works if the husband himself tells the סופר 'Write' and the עדים 'Sign.'
steps.whatsHappening: A brand-new משנה begins. It describes a husband who passed on his instructions through other people, and it rules that the גט does not work.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The problem is not who handed over the גט. Here the husband himself gave it to his wife. The problem is that the סופר and עדים heard the instructions from middlemen and not from the husband himself.

keyTerms.meaning: Scribe, the person who writes the גט
The גט is void and does not work

steps.confusionAlert: Notice that the husband himself gave the גט to his wife, and it is still void. The flaw is only in how the writing and signing were ordered: the instructions passed through middlemen.

phrases.english: MISHNA:
They said to him: Shall we write a bill of divorce for your wife?
And he said to them: Write.
They told the scribe, and he wrote it,
and they told the witnesses, and they signed it;
even though they wrote it and signed it
and gave it to him,
and he then gave it to her,
the bill of divorce is void,
unless he says to the scribe: Write,
and to the witnesses: Sign.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ אָמְרוּ לוֹ: נִכְתּוֹב גֵּט לְאִשְׁתֶּךָ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה. It is not connected to the earlier discussion about a husband who communicates in writing.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If the husband only said 'Write,' and others passed his instructions on to the סופר and עדים, the גט is void unless he instructs them himself.

steps.title: Inference: Saying 'Give' Would Work. Whose View Is That?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא infers that the גט failed only because the husband did not say 'Give'. Had he said 'Give,' the people could pass on the instructions. It asks which תנא holds this.
steps.simpleTranslation: The reason the גט is void is that he did not say 'Give.' But if he had said 'Give,' they could have the גט written and give it. Whose opinion is this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reads between the lines of the משנה's first part and asks which תנא it follows. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The husband only said 'Write,' which does not show he wanted the גט given. So the גמרא infers that if he had said 'Give,' the middlemen could tell the סופר and עדים what to do. That is a specific legal position, so the גמרא asks who holds it.

keyTerms.meaning: Short for גמרא; the discussion of the משנה begins
The reason; often opens an inference from a משנה
'Give!', telling them to give the גט to his wife

phrases.english: GEMARA:
The reason is that he did not say: Give;
but if he said: Give, they may give it.
phrases.notes: He means they may also tell the סופר and עדים to write and sign, and then hand it to her.

phrases.english: Whose opinion is this?

steps.triggerLanguage: טַעְמָא דְּלֹא אָמַר תְּנוּ, הָא אָמַר תְּנוּ נוֹתְנִין, מַנִּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws an inference from the first part of the משנה in Step 9.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which תנא holds that a husband who says 'Give' lets others pass his instructions to the סופר and עדים?

steps.title: The First Part Follows רבי מאיר
steps.stepSummary: The inference matches רבי מאיר, who holds that verbal instructions can be handed over to an agent.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is רבי מאיר, who says that spoken instructions can be handed to an agent.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its question: the first part of the משנה follows רבי מאיר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Everyone agrees that an agent can do an action, like delivering a גט. רבי מאיר goes further: an agent can also pass on spoken instructions, telling a סופר and עדים what to do. That is why 'Give' would be enough.

keyTerms.meaning: Can be handed over to an agent
An agent who acts for someone

steps.whyThisMatters: The idea of מילי מימסרן לשליח, whether spoken instructions can be passed on, is the key idea of this whole סוגיא.

phrases.english: It is Rabbi Meir,
who says: Words can be handed over to an agent.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי מֵאִיר הִיא, דְּאָמַר: מִילֵּי מִימַּסְרָן לְשָׁלִיחַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 10.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The first part of the משנה follows רבי מאיר: spoken instructions can be handed to an agent.

steps.title: But the End of the משנה Follows רבי יוסי
steps.stepSummary: The end of the משנה requires the husband himself to instruct the סופר and עדים. That fits רבי יוסי, who holds that spoken instructions cannot be handed to an agent.
steps.simpleTranslation: Look at the end of the משנה: 'unless he himself says to the סופר: Write, and to the עדים: Sign.' Now we have reached רבי יוסי, who says spoken instructions cannot be handed to an agent.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out that the last line of the משנה seems to follow the opposite opinion, רבי יוסי. This creates a problem that the next step states openly.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ending says the גט only works if the husband personally instructs the סופר and עדים, with no mention of an exception for 'Give.' That sounds like רבי יוסי: instructions can never be passed through an agent. So the two parts of the משנה seem to pull in opposite directions.

keyTerms.meaning: Say (look at) the end of the משנה

phrases.english: Say the latter clause:
Unless he says to the scribe: Write,
and to the witnesses: Sign.
We have arrived at Rabbi Yosei,
who said: Words cannot be handed over to an agent.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵימָא סֵיפָא: עַד שֶׁיֹּאמַר לַסּוֹפֵר כְּתוֹב וְלָעֵדִים חֲתוֹמוּ, אֲתָאן לְרַבִּי יוֹסֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Contrasts the end of the משנה with the first part, which was just tied to רבי מאיר.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the משנה follows רבי מאיר (Step 11).
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ending demands that the husband personally instruct the סופר and עדים. That matches רבי יוסי, the opposite opinion.

steps.title: Can One משנה Follow Two Opposite Views?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא expresses surprise: can the first part follow רבי מאיר and the end follow רבי יוסי?
steps.simpleTranslation: The first part is רבי מאיר and the end is רבי יוסי?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא states the problem out loud: it seems strange for one משנה to switch opinions in the middle.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally we expect a single משנה to follow one consistent view. Splitting it between two opposing תנאים is unusual, so the גמרא asks whether this can really be.

keyTerms.meaning: The first part (beginning) of the משנה
The last part (end) of the משנה

phrases.aramaic: רֵישָׁא רַבִּי מֵאִיר וְסֵיפָא רַבִּי יוֹסֵי?!
phrases.english: The first clause is Rabbi Meir and the latter clause is Rabbi Yosei?!

steps.triggerLanguage: רֵישָׁא רַבִּי מֵאִיר וְסֵיפָא רַבִּי יוֹסֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns the observation of Step 12 into an open challenge.
steps.kashyaTarget: Reading the משנה as split between רבי מאיר and רבי יוסי.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A single משנה should not follow two contradictory opinions.

steps.title: Yes, the משנה Is Split
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא accepts the split: the first part follows רבי מאיר and the end follows רבי יוסי.
steps.simpleTranslation: Yes. The first part is רבי מאיר and the end is רבי יוסי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers simply: yes, this משנה really does follow two different opinions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Instead of forcing both parts into one view, the גמרא accepts that the משנה is split. This is unusual but possible. So the משנה is not one consistent ruling on whether instructions can be passed to an agent.
steps.whatToRemember: Our משנה is split: the inference from the first part (saying 'Give' would work) follows רבי מאיר, who holds instructions can be passed to an agent. The ending (the husband himself must instruct the סופר and עדים) follows רבי יוסי, who holds they cannot.

phrases.english: Yes,

phrases.aramaic: רֵישָׁא רַבִּי מֵאִיר וְסֵיפָא רַבִּי יוֹסֵי.
phrases.english: the first clause is Rabbi Meir and the latter clause is Rabbi Yosei.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִין, רֵישָׁא רַבִּי מֵאִיר וְסֵיפָא רַבִּי יוֹסֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 13 by accepting it.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Accepts the premise: the משנה is split between two תנאים.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: One would think a single משנה must follow one consistent opinion.
steps.terutzMaskana: This משנה really does follow רבי מאיר in its first part and רבי יוסי in its last part.

steps.title: אביי: The whole משנה follows רבי מאיר
steps.stepSummary: אביי rejects the split. He says the whole משנה follows רבי מאיר, and the end is talking about a husband who never said 'Give'.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: The whole משנה is רבי מאיר. The end is talking about a case where the husband did not say 'Give.'
steps.whatsHappening: אביי offers a new way to solve the problem from step 13. He says there is no need to split the משנה between two תנאים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר holds that instructions can be passed on, but only when the husband said 'Give' the גט. אביי explains that in the end of the משנה the husband only said 'Write', so he has to instruct the סופר and עדים himself. That way the end also fits רבי מאיר.

keyTerms.meaning: Here, what case are we dealing with? This introduces a narrower reading of the case

steps.confusionAlert: אביי is not agreeing with step 14. He is offering a different approach, so the משנה would not need to be split.

phrases.english: Abaye said:
All of it is Rabbi Meir,
and here, with what are we dealing?
Where he did not say "Give."

steps.triggerLanguage: אַבָּיֵי אָמַר: כּוּלָּהּ רַבִּי מֵאִיר הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers an alternative to the split accepted in step 14
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The end of the משנה, which requires the husband himself to instruct, must follow רבי יוסי
steps.terutzMaskana: The end follows רבי מאיר too, because it deals with a husband who did not say 'Give'

steps.title: Then the משנה should have said 'until he says Give'
steps.stepSummary: If the problem is that he did not say 'Give', the משנה should have said 'until he says Give'.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, the משנה should have said: 'until he says Give!'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges אביי's reading from the wording of the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says 'until he says' to the סופר 'write'. If the missing piece were the word 'Give', the משנה would have named that word. Since it did not, אביי's case does not match the wording.

phrases.english: If so,
it should have said "until he says 'Give'"!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי הָכִי, עַד שֶׁיֹּאמַר תְּנוּ מִיבְּעֵי לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks אביי's first case from step 15
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading that the husband did not say 'Give'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה's wording 'until he says' would have named the missing word 'Give' if that were the issue

steps.title: The husband did not speak to three people
steps.stepSummary: A new case: the husband gave his instructions to only two people, not to three.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the case is where he did not say it to a group of three.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries a different case to keep the whole משנה under רבי מאיר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Three people form a בית דין, and a בית דין can appoint others to write the גט. Two people are not a בית דין, so they cannot pass the job on, even if the husband said 'Give'. That would explain why the husband has to instruct the סופר and עדים himself.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, which drops the previous answer
A group of three, which can act as a בית דין

phrases.english: Rather, here, with what are we dealing?
Where he did not say it to a group of three.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא הָכָא בְּמַאי עָסְקִינַן דְּלָא אֲמַר לְבֵי תְלָתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejected case from step 15 with a new case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The case is about not saying 'Give', but that does not fit the wording
steps.terutzMaskana: The case is where the husband instructed only two people, who cannot appoint others

steps.title: Then the משנה should have said 'to three'
steps.stepSummary: If the issue is speaking to three, the משנה should have said 'until he says it to three'.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, the משנה should have said: 'until he says it to three!'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא uses the same wording challenge again, this time against the 'three people' case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה stresses that the husband must speak to the סופר and עדים themselves. If the real requirement were speaking to a group of three, the משנה would have said so. So this case also does not match the wording.

phrases.english: If so,
it should have said "until he says it to three"!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי הָכִי, עַד שֶׁיֹּאמַר לִשְׁלֹשָׁה מִיבְּעֵי לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the case from step 17 with the same wording argument
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading that the husband did not speak to three
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If three people were the requirement, the משנה would have said 'to three'

steps.title: The whole משנה follows רבי יוסי
steps.stepSummary: A switch: the whole משנה is רבי יוסי, and the beginning deals with a husband who did not say 'Say'.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the whole משנה is רבי יוסי. The case is where the husband did not say 'Say.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives up on putting the whole משנה under רבי מאיר. Now it tries to put the whole משנה under רבי יוסי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוסי holds that spoken instructions cannot simply be handed to an agent. The suggestion is that the husband failed because he never told the people 'Say' my instructions to the סופר. This reading makes the whole משנה fit רבי יוסי.

phrases.english: Rather, all of it is Rabbi Yosei,
and here, with what are we dealing?
Where he did not say "Say."

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא כּוּלַּהּ רַבִּי יוֹסֵי הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Abandons the רבי מאיר approach and tries to put the whole משנה under רבי יוסי
steps.terutzResolutionType: Switching the attribution plus narrowing the case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The whole משנה could be explained as רבי מאיר
steps.terutzMaskana: The whole משנה is רבי יוסי, and the case is where the husband did not say 'Say'

steps.title: Then the משנה should have said 'until he says Say'
steps.stepSummary: If the problem is that he did not say 'Say', the משנה should have said 'until he says Say'.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, the משנה should have said: 'until he says Say!'
steps.whatsHappening: The same wording challenge now hits the רבי יוסי reading.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the missing word were 'Say', the משנה would have named it. Instead it says 'until he says' to the סופר directly. So this reading also does not fit the exact language.

phrases.english: If so,
it should have said "until he says 'Say'"!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי הָכִי, עַד שֶׁיֹּאמַר אִמְרוּ מִיבְּעֵי לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the רבי יוסי reading from step 19 with the same wording argument
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading that the husband did not say 'Say'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה would have named the missing word 'Say' if that were the issue

steps.title: Does רבי יוסי even accept 'Say'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא raises a second problem: it is not clear that רבי יוסי agrees that saying 'Say' works at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: Furthermore, does רבי יוסי really agree in a case where the husband says 'Say'?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds another attack on the answer from Step 19. It asks whether רבי יוסי agrees that a husband's instruction 'Say' works at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 19 said the whole משנה follows רבי יוסי, and that the problem in the opening case was only that the husband did not say 'Say.' That answer quietly assumes that, for רבי יוסי, saying 'Say' would have made things fine. The גמרא now doubts this assumption, and it will bring a source to show it.

keyTerms.meaning: Furthermore, and another thing: introduces an extra challenge
Does he really agree? (asked with disbelief)

phrases.english: Furthermore,
does Rabbi Yosei really agree
in the case of one who says 'Say'?!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְעוֹד, מִי מוֹדֶה רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּאוֹמֵר: ״אִמְרוּ״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second challenge to the answer in Step 19, alongside the wording problem raised in Step 20.
steps.kashyaTarget: The assumption in Step 19 that, for רבי יוסי, a husband who says 'Say' has validly arranged the גט.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If רבי יוסי does not accept 'Say' at all, then the opening of the משנה cannot be explained as a case where the husband merely failed to say 'Say.'

steps.title: A משנה about a scribe and one witness
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא cites a משנה that validates a גט with a scribe and one witness, and רבי ירמיה explains that the scribe there signed it.
steps.simpleTranslation: But we learned in a משנה: 'A scribe wrote, and one witness, it is valid.' And רבי ירמיה said: we learned 'a scribe signed.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts building its proof by quoting a משנה and רבי ירמיה's correction of its wording. This step sets up the source that the next step will use against רבי יוסי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says a גט with a scribe and one witness is valid. רבי ירמיה says we should read it as the scribe signing the גט as a witness, not just writing it. So the case is a scribe and one more witness signing together. This background is needed for רב חסדא's comment that follows.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not read 'כתב סופר' as 'the scribe wrote the גט.' רבי ירמיה says the משנה is about the scribe signing it as a witness.

phrases.english: But didn't we learn in a Mishnah:
'A scribe wrote, and a witness, it is valid';
phrases.notes: This is the משנה on 87b: a גט that has the scribe and just one witness on it.

phrases.english: and Rabbi Yirmeya said:
we learned 'a scribe signed.'
phrases.notes: He means the scribe signed as one of the two witnesses. He did not just write the גט.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָתְנַן: ״כָּתַב סוֹפֵר וְעֵד – כָּשֵׁר״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings the source that will back up the doubt raised in Step 21.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי יוסי does not accept a husband's instruction 'Say.'
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה on 87b (a scribe and one witness), as read by רבי ירמיה: the scribe signed.

steps.title: רב חסדא asks whose view the משנה follows
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא asks which תנא the scribe-and-witness משנה follows. His answer comes on the next עמוד.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב חסדא said: whose view is this משנה?
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא begins identifying the author of the scribe-and-witness משנה. This line sets up his answer, which comes at the start of the next עמוד.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once we know which תנא the משנה follows, the גמרא can show what that תנא holds about passing on spoken instructions. That will decide whether רבי יוסי could accept 'Say.' The question is the hinge of the proof.

keyTerms.meaning: Whose is it? Which תנא said it?

phrases.english: And Rav Chisda said:
whose view is this Mishnah? —
phrases.notes: רב חסדא is asking this so he can answer it himself. His answer comes at the start of the next עמוד.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא: מַתְנִיתִין מַנִּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the proof from Step 22 by asking who authored that משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which תנא the scribe-and-one-witness משנה follows. The answer will show whether רבי יוסי accepts 'Say.'
